evidence: a-run-writes-a-restorable-gzip-tar: backup.sh.erb:14-20 sets COMPRESSION_FLAG=z unless COMPRESSION is false; with the default compression=true line 31 runs tar -cvzf into BACKDIR/FILEPREFIX-<date +%Y-%b-%d-%Hh%Mm>.tar.gz, so a gzip-valid p8test-backup-DATE.tar.gz holding etc/default (tar strips the leading /) from which etc/default/cron restores identically is what the code produces; the effect re-tests the archive (gzip -t, cmp of the restored file), not the script's output

script-installed-with-the-parameters: backup.sh.erb:15 renders COMPRESSION=<%= @compression %>, which with the default Boolean true is COMPRESSION=true; lines 4-7 render FILETARGETDIRS/FILEPREFIX/BACKDIR/NC from the params fixture (/etc/default, p8test-backup, /opt/puppet-infrastructure/backup, 7) and manifests/backup.pp:14-19 gives root:root 0755 at bindir/backup-backup.sh; the expectation matches

a-run-deletes-only-its-own-old-archives: backup.sh.erb:22-23 gives DAYS=INTERVAL(1)*NC(7)-1=6, and lines 35-37 rm files found by find BACKDIR -maxdepth 1 -mtime +6 -name 'p8test-backup*'; so the 8-day-old p8test-backup-old is removed, the 3-day-old p8test-backup-recent stays, and p8test-other-old (30 days, not matching the prefix) stays; the new archive remains; expected listing is exactly that. The backup directory comes from filesystem_base (the plan's required_base), not from the planting step
